hypothesis: H-FUNDCLOCK: funding-settlement clock pressure on Binance USDT-M perps
status_at_freeze: No price, P&L or exit outcome computed. No kline or funding data for this hypothesis downloaded yet. Only file sizes of BTCUSDT/WIFUSDT 1m monthly zips were listed (S3 listing) to plan the download budget.
mechanism: Traders who would pay funding at settlement T close just before T and reopen after T. With funding strongly positive, longs exit pre-settlement (down pressure in the last minutes) and re-enter after (up pressure); mirror for negative funding.

source_leads.ref: He, Manela, Ross, von Wachter, 'Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures', arXiv 2212.06888
source_leads.use: funding mechanism (longs pay shorts when perp > spot); no settlement-clock price claim

source_leads.ref: 'Temporal Dynamics of Market Microstructure in Cryptocurrency Perpetual Futures', Int. J. Financial Studies 14(5):103 (MDPI), https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7072/14/5/103
source_leads.use: search-result snippet only (page returned HTTP 403): funding-rate spreads reported to peak ~2h after standard settlement times (02:00/10:00/18:00 UTC). Not verified, not about price.

source_leads.ref: Binance Square practitioner posts on funding (https://www.binance.com/square/post/28903286409497) and Binance funding schedule 00/08/16 UTC
source_leads.use: practitioner framing that traders manage positions around funding; no quantified price pattern
no published study quantifying minute-level price pressure just before / after funding settlement was found; the hypothesis is therefore practitioner folklore, tested here from scratch

splits.boundary: a trade belongs to the split of its settlement time T (train: T < 2025-07-01 00:00 UTC; validation: 2025-07-01 00:00 <= T <= 2026-03-31 23:59). Windows are within [T-30m, T+31m], so a PRE trade for T = 2025-07-01 00:00 reads only 2025-06-30 prices but belongs to validation, and no train trade reads validation prices (last train T = 2025-06-30 23:00 at most, exit <= 23:31). Validation T after 2026-03-31 23:00 are excluded so nothing reads 2026-04 prices.

universe.rule: For each calendar month M (2023-01..2026-03), the top 20 Binance USDT-M perpetual symbols (name ends with USDT, no '_' delivery suffix) by summed quote volume in month M-1 from data.binance.vision futures/um/monthly/klines/<SYM>/1d, with >=28 daily rows in M-1, excluding stablecoin/fiat bases (USDC, FDUSD, TUSD, BUSD, USDP, DAI, EUR, AEUR, USDE, PYUSD, USD1, UST, USTC). Point in time (uses only M-1). Majors (BTC, ETH) are included.
universe.reason_for_N: download budget: ~1.85 MB per symbol-month 1m zip; 20 x 39 months ~ 1.45 GB streamed, nothing stored but window extracts
universe.missing_data: a member whose 1m kline or fundingRate file for M is missing is dropped for M and reported

data.klines: futures/um/monthly/klines/<SYM>/1m (streamed, only bars within [T-35m, T+35m] of each settlement kept)
data.funding: futures/um/monthly/fundingRate/<SYM> (calc_time, rate). Settlement times T are the calc_time values floored to the minute; these follow Binance's published schedule (8h, or 4h/1h on symbols with other intervals), which is known in advance.

signal.PRE: f = the most recent SETTLED funding rate before T (the print at the previous settlement). Fully point in time at T-k. The not-yet-settled rate at T is NOT used. Correlation of f with the rate at T is reported as a diagnostic only.
signal.POST: f = the rate settled at T (published at T; trade enters at T+1 min).

trade_rule.PRE: if f >= +thr: SHORT (against the paying long side, which is expected to sell before T); if f <= -thr: LONG. Entry at the OPEN of the 1m bar starting at T-k; exit at the CLOSE of the 1m bar starting at T-1 (i.e. strictly before settlement, no funding exchanged).
trade_rule.POST: if f >= +thr: LONG (paying longs re-enter after T); if f <= -thr: SHORT. Entry at the OPEN of the 1m bar starting at T+1 min (strictly after settlement, no funding exchanged); exit at the CLOSE of the bar starting at T+m (hold ~m minutes).
trade_rule.max_trades: 1 trade per symbol per settlement per config
trade_rule.missing_bars: if an entry or exit bar is missing the trade is skipped and counted

costs.fee_source: Binance USDS-M regular-user taker 0.05% (Binance FAQ 360033544231, as cited in reports/failures/agent_premconv.md)
costs.maker_variant: NOT run: modelling maker non-fill honestly would need queue/tick data; the taker-only cost is primary and only cost model

pnl: per trade, fraction of notional: side * (exit/entry - 1) - 0.0014. Split totals reported as sums in % of notional.
bar: per split: n >= 50, net sum > 0, PF > 1.2, net sum without the 3 best trades > 0
selection: Run all 12 configs on train. Among configs meeting the bar on train, pick ONE: the highest train net sum (ties: higher PF). That single config is run on validation once. If no config meets the train bar, validation is not run (protocol precedent: agent_flush, agent_premconv) and the verdict is FAIL. No re-tuning; any variant needs a new pre-registration.
reporting: per split: n, net sum %, mean bp, PF, net ex-top3, win rate, by year, by symbol (top contributors and share of net), top days, day-clustered t; gross (pre-cost) mean as a diagnostic of whether any pressure exists at all.
